Aromatic Cosmetics Ltd ------- Petitioners
Vs.
Commissioner, Customs, Excise and VAT Commissionerate and ors. ------- Respondents
full_judgment: 25. Thus reading section 40 with sections 20 and 21 of the Act and Rule 6 of the VAT Rules, it can very well be determined that the Divisional Officer being subordinate to the Commissioner his functions can be performed by the Commissioner. Moreover, the Commissioner having dual power of confiscation and imposition of fine he can use either of the two or both. On application of the aforesaid sections and Rule 6, his exercising the power of imposing fine will not be overstepping the powers of the Divisional Officer. So, in this regard, we respectfully disagree with the view taken by their Lordships in the case of Opsonin vs Director Customs Intelligence and others referred above and the observation that section 21 merely creates obligation in the superior officer to ensure performance of the powers and functions entrusted to or conferred on him by law and not to perform the powers and functions of the subordinate officers by himself and thereby making the subordinate officer an otiose and redundant and the same will create anarchy, indiscipline and dissatisfaction in the rank and file among the VAT officers.' The language of section 21(1) is clear in this respect. In fiscal law statute is to be interpreted on the language used in the statute, it is merely to see what is clearly stated therein, there is no scope for any intendment nor for any equity or presumption. Thus the language used in section 21 gives a clear meaning that the officers as mentioned in section 20 can exercise and perform the powers and functions entrusted upon any of his subordinate officers. So, reading section 40 together with sections 20, 21 and Rule 6 it will be clear that the Commissioner having dual power of confiscation and fine under his own capacity can exercise both, side by side he can also exercise either of the two. Thus the power of imposing fine only, upon exercising his own power as well as the powers of his subordinate i.e. the Divisional Officer, the Commissioner has not acted illegally. Under such circumstances the term "and" used in section 40 (খ)(অ) is to be read disjunctively. Accordingly, the actions taken by the Commissioner in passing the impugned orders of adjudication is not beyond his jurisdiction, rather the same are passed within the purview of law and, as such, the impugned orders are found to have been passed n accordance with law.
